Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

- **kagex-release** packages a game for Windows, Linux, Linux for Steam, macOS, the web, Android and iOS from one settings window (or `--cli build`). It's in the Windows and Linux zips as `tools/kagex-release`, and on its own for each system (`kagex-release-windows.zip`, `kagex-release-linux.tar.gz`, `kagex-release-macos.zip`). It can convert WAV and FLAC to Opus or Ogg Vorbis and PNG, BMP and TLG images to TLG6 on the way, shows what your computer can build, and test-runs the result. [tools/release/README.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.3.0/tools/release/README.md) describes every setting
- `kagex_engine_*.zip` are the engines it packages with; it downloads the ones it needs by itself
- The framework finds `.opus` sounds named without their extension, like `.wav` and `.ogg`
- The Android app is named KAGEX Sample on Japanese and Chinese phones too

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.3.0/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tool aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tool, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
